industry.why: Neutral, carried, balanced on new evidence both ways. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): two houses call a cyclical upturn, DNB Carnegie (22 Oct) reading Sandvik and Metso as a new mining cycle and Danske (18 Oct) heavy trucks and pulp and paper turning, and Goldman's economists (16 Oct) have US industrial production beating with machinery and electrical equipment near peak capacity use; against it, Danske's own warning that most cyclical exposure is 'more or less at all-time highs' with 'cost inflation emerging', a risk-off regime confirmed on all five defensive windows, and Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: D now, C prior at industry level. The sector rows do the work: Electrical equipment and grid, Diversified groups, Distributors and Test and measurement at C, Flow control and Building technology at D. Counter-case for B: the order data are the strongest non-AI demand read in the pack; for D: the tape and the regime.

Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-16 against 2026-08-14, not week on week: D now, D prior, agrees. Counter-case: 26 stocks of mixed character, energy-efficiency retrofit demand benefits from the energy shock, British Land beat with 3 to 5% rental growth guidance, and rate-sensitive groups are where a relief rally starts; no MI Pool name sits in this row. Back to C if the Fed path is marked down.

memo.verdict: Park. Neutral on the shares at EUR 27.95 on 2026-10-01; bullish on the business. Carel Industries (CRL-IT) is a demand-inflection case in a high-quality HVAC/R controls niche, already delivered in the numbers and already paid for in the price: the modal total shareholder return with the 24-month-forward multiple held at today's 27.6 times is about 12.5 percent a year over eighteen months and 11.1 percent a year over three years against the 20 percent bar, a D on the framework's anchors. Two triggers: a price near EUR 24, where the modal path clears the bar (EUR 25.4 at eighteen months, EUR 22.2 at three years); and the Q3 2026 print on 12-Nov-26, which would move the modal path up if North American HVAC grows at 30 percent or more and the EBITDA margin holds above 22 percent, in which case the clearing price rises toward EUR 26 to 27. Conviction: medium on the business, a working hypothesis on the return. The gate does not park the case (management B, business quality B, predictability B, trackability C); the price does. Invalidation thresholds: group organic growth below 10 percent for two quarters; EBITDA margin below 20 percent for two quarters; working capital above 25 percent of sales for two quarters.
case: - The thesis: Carel is a demand-inflection case in a high-quality controls niche, already delivered in the numbers and already paid for in the price. Two structural forces (AI data-centre cooling in North America and the UK; the European F-Gas shift to natural refrigerants) joined a cyclical recovery in European residential heat pumps to lift organic growth to 23.0 percent and the EBITDA margin to 22.5 percent in H1 2026, above the company's 19 to 20 percent frame; the business case is compelling, the share-price case at EUR 27.95 is not.

- The change is external, structural in two of three legs, and sector-wide. North American revenues up 55.7 percent at constant currency with data-centre revenues nearly doubling; BELIMO's data-centre revenues up 93 percent in local currency; refrigeration organic growth above 30 percent in Q2 2026 under the revised EU F-Gas regulation (published 20-Feb-24, high-GWP phase-out by 2030); residential heat pumps close to 30 percent in early 2026, concentrated in Germany and Northern Europe; Trane's backlog USD 10.70bn; Lennox confirming residential distributor destocking ended early Q2 2026. Internal forces are second-order: a flatter structure after the Managing Director's retirement, a new chief technology officer, bolt-ons (Kiona 2023, Cotes 2026), the North Carolina plant, incentives moved to cash flow; no chief-executive change, no guidance step-up.

- The change has travelled the whole 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain, which is why it is material rather than promised: actions, operating metrics (organic growth 23.0 percent, margin 22.5 percent), financial statements (net profit up 72.5 percent to EUR 45.7m), and sell-side estimates (FY2026 EPS up 25.7 percent and FY2027 up 21.6 percent over twelve months; all seven visible brokers' estimates dated 30-Jul-26 to 17-Sep-26, after the H1 print; the consensus mean from a twelve-month low of EUR 0.644 to EUR 0.816 at the series high).
counter_case: - At its strongest: Carel's H1 2026 is the top of a cycle, not the start of one. The growth is a cyclical rebound plus a data-centre spike read as structural. Residential heat pumps are rebounding from a destocked trough on restored German subsidies that politics can remove, and the same lever cut group revenue 11 percent in 2024. EMEA refrigeration above 30 percent in Q2 2026 may be delayed projects catching up, a one-off. North American data-centre cooling is a capital-spending boom into which the large competitors (Trane, Carrier, Johnson Controls, Vertiv, Schneider) are arriving, and hyperscalers can pause orders with three weeks' notice; Munters has already guided its data-centre margin down to 17.5 to 18 percent on competition and missed data-centre sales by 15 percent on US ramp delays; hyperscaler certification cycles run up to twelve months; the exposure is concentrated in one region.

- Visibility is three to five weeks. Two-thirds of sales go through OEMs who alter their monthly schedules, and distributors manage inventory with extreme caution. The 22.5 percent margin is volume on 15 plants of fixed cost and reverses with volume as it did in 2024 (21.1 to 18.1 percent); growth was almost entirely volume-driven, so a volume pause de-leverages at about 4 percent of EPS per 2 points of volume, with memory-chip inflation (DRAM up six-fold) and US plant start-up costs in 2027 on top.
triggers: - Price trigger: about EUR 24 (EUR 25.4 on the eighteen-month arithmetic, EUR 22.2 on the three-year), below the 200-day average of EUR 25.94 and near the April 2026 level of about EUR 23.7; the case progresses there on the modal path.

- Q3 2026 print on 12-Nov-26: the Q3 guide of about EUR 190m (roughly 20 percent up) against the outturn; North American HVAC growth at 30 percent or more (Alarm below 30 percent in a quarter); EMEA refrigeration organic growth above 15 percent (Alarm below 15 percent in a quarter; Invalidate below 15 percent for two quarters); EBITDA margin above 22 percent to lift the modal path (Alarm below 21 percent in a quarter; Invalidate below 20 percent for two quarters); the reported H2 EPS comparison will look flat against the option-gain-flattered H2 2025 base, a presentational risk.

- Group invalidation thresholds: organic growth below 10 percent for two quarters; EBITDA margin below 20 percent for two quarters; working capital above 25 percent of sales for two quarters (Alarm above 22 percent); net cash before IFRS 16 not worse than minus EUR 20m; inventory toward 15 to 17 percent of sales by Q4 2026.

- Multiple: Alarm at the 35th percentile, 26.9 times; a de-rating toward Epiroc's 24 times would be the quality-industrial level if the data-centre premium faded; the Invalidate level is an earnings cut, not a price level.

- Policy: a German or Northern European heat-pump subsidy amendment tabled is the Alarm; the Cyber Resilience Act (reporting from 11-Sep-26, CE marking by 11-Dec-27) and a possible PFAS restriction add cost; carbon pricing and CBAM on imported components are a cost risk from 2027.

- Peers and read-across: BELIMO's and Munters' data-centre growth and any hyperscaler capital-spending pause reported by a large cooling supplier; Section 232 tariff changes; a Carrier-type margin-mix disappointment in the sector.
